artifacts.summary: Audits the four Check-8 coarse file_scope declarations (177 Decidability/, 282/296/298 BimodalTools/) and the Check-9 duplicate (178), recommending narrowing for 282/296/298, an inline justification plus a missing dependency edge (696) for 177, --fix for 178, confirming no further check-module-invariants.sh additions are evidenced, flagging project 412's missing file_scope as the most relevant residue, and recording the postflight-gating follow-on for the separate agent-system repository.

memory_candidates.content: In this repo, validate-state.sh's Check 8 (coarse file_scope) only fires on directory-ending entries with >=3 overlapping non-terminal tasks (FILE_SCOPE_COARSE_MIN_OVERLAP, default 3); a missing/null file_scope is invisible to the same overlap predicate (scopes_overlap_first treats an absent array as empty, so it never overlaps anything) and is therefore a strictly worse, silent version of the same hazard a coarse directory declaration at least surfaces as a WARN. When auditing file_scope hygiene, missing/null declarations on tasks that plausibly touch a known shared serialization point (e.g. scripts/check-module-invariants.sh's AXIOM_BASELINE) deserve priority over merely-coarse ones.

scripts/check-module-invariants.sh's C2 check pins a hardcoded AXIOM_BASELINE heredoc (theorem name -> expected axiom list) for flagship/certificate-stack theorems; a task that lands a new flagship theorem worth axiom-pinning (and a matching docs/theorem-index.md row, per C15) should declare scripts/check-module-invariants.sh and docs/theorem-index.md in its file_scope, as tasks 695/696 already correctly do. A task merely gated by an EXISTING check-module-invariants.sh check ('no regression to any currently-passing check') is not itself an editor of the script and should not have it added to file_scope on that basis alone.

orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh (agent-system source-store repo, extensions/core/scripts/) already computes a modified_files-vs-declared-file_scope excursion at WORK (h), lines ~1053-1069, but only logs it to stderr as an ADVISORY with 'no gate, no exit-code, no verdict effect'. Any future task to make file_scope enforcement actually load-bearing should build on this existing detection logic (which is already correct) rather than re-deriving the comparison; the gap is purely in the consequence, not the detection.
